subject.title: [Bug]: sanitizeForPromptLiteral destructively strips tabs and newlines

question: Should escaped tagged prompt-data blocks preserve raw horizontal tabs, render tabs as a safe visible representation, or remain intentionally lossy?
rationale: Current source and tests define control-character stripping as prompt-injection hardening, so altering the allowed whitespace set requires explicit ownership of the security tradeoff.

options.title: Separate block sanitizer
options.body: Preserve normalized LF and reviewed horizontal whitespace only inside escaped tagged blocks while keeping inline literals strict.

options.title: Escape tabs visibly
options.body: Represent tabs with a safe visible sequence inside tagged blocks instead of retaining raw control characters.

options.title: Keep lossy behavior
options.body: Retain tab stripping and document that fidelity-sensitive callers must encode or normalize their input first.

recommendation.title: Separate block sanitizer
recommendation.body: Preserve normalized LF and reviewed horizontal whitespace only inside escaped tagged blocks while keeping inline literals strict.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the strict sanitizer contract and is the strongest available owner for deciding whether raw tabs fit this boundary.
